product.amstrad-pc5286.summary: The 286 model in the Series 5 combined office work with an optional Games Pack for home gaming.
product.amstrad-pc5286.history: Documented in the August 1991 brochure, the PC5286 was the 286 alternative to the PC5086 in the Series 5: a compact desktop aimed at professional work, with Counterpoint for using DOS through a mouse. The Games Pack brought that machine into the home with sound, speakers, a joystick and games; the British advertisement priced it at £899 excluding VAT on 1 October 1991. The brochure states that it was designed in the United Kingdom and manufactured in Taiwan, Korea or the United Kingdom.
product.amstrad-pc5286.warning: Experimental emulation: boot, memory and video have been tested, but the factory hard disk, keyboard controller and original sound card are not yet reproduced with full fidelity.
Floppy model — no hard disk or sound card
Games Pack — 40 MB IDE and AdLib-compatible sound
product.amstrad-pc5286.creation.note: Internal VGA and all listed RAM populations are validated. The 40 MB image uses a period-compatible CP346 geometry because the exact factory drive is not identified. Games Pack sound uses generic AdLib emulation; its integrated game port is not yet modelled.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.market: Amstrad offered it for work and play. British brochures from August and September 1991 document the professional machine and Games Pack; the £899 price excluding VAT comes from the October advertisement.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.commerc: It could be bought with or without a hard disk. Documented choices include one 1.44 MB floppy drive, the 40 MB IDE option and the Games Pack; 1 MB RAM could be expanded to 2 or 4 MB.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.accesso: The Games Pack added sound and game controls. It included an Amstrad AdLib-compatible card, two speakers, an AJ-5 joystick, Links, F-15 Strike Eagle II and Prince of Persia.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.cpu: The 286 processor distinguished it from the PC5086. The manual specifies 16 MHz, two 16-bit ISA slots and a socket for an optional 80287 coprocessor.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.memory: Memory could be expanded for more demanding software. The manual documents 80 ns SIMMs installed in pairs, with 1, 2 or 4 MB configurations; the 512 KB memory map does not establish a commercially sold version.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.chipset: Two chips handle memory and peripheral control. The owner's report identifies C&T F82C235-12 and F82C710A; it is not a substitute for a board schematic.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.video: VGA is built into the motherboard. Photographs of the MC0128A show a C&T F82C452, ADV476KP35E RAMDAC and eight D41464C-10 DRAMs, equivalent to 256 KiB; this is not extended to every revision.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.storage: The hard disk was an option for storing programs and data. Sales material documents 40 MB IDE alongside a 1.44 MB floppy drive; the exact hard disk model remains unidentified.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.interfa: Common peripherals could connect without additional cards. The brochure lists RS-232C serial, bidirectional parallel, VGA and PS/2-type keyboard and mouse connectors.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.firmwar: ROMs are preserved for studying startup and video. The files identify AM52V004, 64 KiB, and C&T VGA Version 220, 32 KiB; original bytes are preserved without redistribution.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.verifie: Earlier BluMach tests cover startup and several basic functions. Records include POST, saved Setup settings, 1/2/4 MB RAM, shadow/remapping, EMS with SCATEMM 1.4, VGA and BIOS modes 63h/64h.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.limitat: The model remains experimental and uses approximations. KBC/NVR and IDE are generic; the disk uses 805/4/26 geometry and the Games Pack uses AdLib without its game port. The dump needs an optional in-memory checksum correction; advanced timing and the VGA cursor require comparison with physical hardware.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.brochur: Sales material documents positioning and price. PC5286 and Games Pack brochures, August/September 1991; Amstrad advertisement with prices valid on 1 October 1991, preserved from CPCrulez.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.manual: The manual distinguishes the two machines and their upgrades. PC5086/PC5286 User Manual, PC Guide 1-3/1-4, 7-2 and 8-9/8-10; the service manual remains pending.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.firmwar: The dump has an identified provenance. FreddyV supplied the system and VGA ROMs published by Banjo; the local record preserves originals and hashes.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.sound_c: Photographs identify the components of one particular unit. MC0128A board published by Ikesankom in 2017 during a repair; factory wiring is not assumed to remain entirely intact.
